name: Delenta
tagline: All-in-one platform for coaches: client management, scheduling, payments, program delivery and a branded client portal.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Delenta is a bundle, not an algorithm: bookings, client records, session notes, packages with session credits, invoices, a client-facing portal and some landing page tooling. Every single piece of that is standard CRUD that an agent can scaffold, and a solo coach with ten to thirty clients genuinely does not need a platform to track them. The gaps are the boring plumbing: Stripe checkout and refunds, Google Calendar two-way sync, timezone math that does not embarrass you in front of a paying client, reminder emails that actually land, and a video call link per session. You can get a working local version in a weekend and a version you would let clients log into after a few more evenings. If you are a coaching business with multiple coaches, shared availability and revenue splits, stop reading and keep paying.
coreLoopDIY: A single-coach web app where clients book from your real availability, you log session notes against their record, and packages burn down session credits with Stripe-paid invoices attached.
requirements: Node 20 and a place to run it (a small VPS or Fly/Render box)
Stripe account for payments and a webhook endpoint
Google Cloud project with Calendar API credentials if you want two-way calendar sync
Transactional email provider (Resend or Postmark) for booking confirmations and reminders
A domain, because clients will not click a bare IP address
whatYouLose: Payments and tax handling you did not have to think about: Stripe webhooks, failed cards, refunds and partial package refunds are all now your bugs
Reliable reminder delivery, which is mostly deliverability reputation rather than code
Mobile access for you and your clients that feels like an app instead of a cramped web page
Prebuilt landing pages, lead capture and the marketing side of the bundle
Multi-coach support: shared availability, assignment, per-coach reporting and payouts
moatNotes: The lock-in is not clever software, it is calendars, Stripe accounts, historic session notes and clients who already know where to log in.
whyPeopleStillPay: Coaches sell hours, and every hour spent debugging a timezone bug or a failed Stripe webhook is an hour not billed. The bundle is the product: one monthly fee replaces a booking tool, an invoicing tool, a notes doc, a client portal and a reminder system, each of which would otherwise need wiring together and babysitting. There is also a trust layer that is hard to fake alone: clients expect to pay through something that looks like a real business, not a self-hosted form on a subdomain. Self-hosting makes sense if you are technical, your client list is small and you mostly want your notes and schedule to stop fighting you.
notes: Nothing here is hard, there is just a lot of it, and the last twenty percent is all payments and email deliverability.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted coaching practice manager for a single coach. No multi-tenant, no team features, no marketing site builder.

Stack, non-negotiable: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript), SQLite via Prisma, Tailwind, server actions. Run it with `npm run dev` locally and as a single Node process in production. No external auth provider.

Two surfaces in one app:
1. Coach admin at /admin, protected by a single password from COACH_PASSWORD in .env, stored in an httpOnly session cookie.
2. Client portal at /c/[token], where each client gets an unguessable link token. No client passwords.

Data model: Client (name, email, timezone, notes, archived), Package (client, name, totalSessions, sessionsUsed, priceCents, status), Session (client, startsAt UTC, durationMins, status: scheduled/completed/no-show/cancelled, meetingUrl, privateNotes, sharedNotes, packageId nullable), AvailabilityRule (weekday, startTime, endTime, timezone), Blackout (start, end, reason), Invoice (client, packageId, amountCents, stripeCheckoutId, status).

Features, in scope:
- Availability editor: weekly recurring windows plus one-off blackouts, all entered in the coach timezone from COACH_TZ.
- Public booking at /c/[token]/book: shows open slots in the client's stored timezone, derived from availability minus existing sessions minus blackouts. Store everything in UTC, render with date-fns-tz. Write a test for the slot generator across a DST boundary.
- Session credits: booking against an active package increments sessionsUsed; cancelling more than 24h out refunds the credit.
- Session notes: privateNotes visible only in /admin, sharedNotes visible in the client portal.
- Stripe Checkout for packages: a server action creates a Checkout Session, a /api/stripe/webhook route verifies the signature and marks the Invoice paid and the Package active. Keys in .env.
- Email via Resend: booking confirmation, cancellation, and a 24h reminder. Reminders run from a /api/cron/reminders route guarded by a CRON_SECRET header, called by an external cron.
- Admin dashboard: today's sessions, packages running low on credits, unpaid invoices.
- CSV export of clients and sessions.

Explicitly out of scope: video hosting (paste a meeting URL per session), landing pages, lead forms, group coaching, multiple coaches, in-app chat, analytics, telemetry of any kind.

Deliver a seed script with two fake clients and one package, a README covering .env vars and the cron setup, and no secrets committed.
